entry.title: Taskbar Mini Folders 1.0.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Mini Folders

Adds mini folders to the Windows 11 taskbar, like the app folders on a phone. Each mini folder is a small tile that shows the first four icons inside it. Click the tile and a panel opens above the taskbar with everything in the folder. Click an icon to launch it.

Use it to group apps (Work, Games, Tools) and keep the taskbar short.

How it works

Every mini folder is a real folder on disk. By default it is %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders\<folder name>. The mod creates the folder the first time you use + Add... or Open folder in it, not before. Whatever is in that folder shows up in the mini folder: shortcuts, programs, files and other folders. Hidden and system files are skipped. Items are sorted by name.

Using it

Action Result
Click a mini folder Opens its panel. Click it again, press Esc or click elsewhere to close the panel
Click an icon in the panel Opens the app, file or folder
Right-click an icon Open, Open file location, Remove from this folder (Delete for real files and folders)
+ Add... Pick apps or files. A shortcut to each one is created in the folder
Open folder Opens the folder in Explorer, so you can drag items in, rename or delete them

"Remove from this folder" sends a shortcut to the Recycle Bin without asking. For a real file or folder (not a shortcut) the menu item is called "Delete", because it removes the real item: it goes to the Recycle Bin, and Windows may ask you to confirm first. On a drive without a Recycle Bin (for example a network drive) the item is deleted permanently, and Windows asks first.

The file picker of + Add... starts in the Start menu programs folder, where most installed apps have a shortcut.

Settings

Setting Default What it does
Mini folders Apps, Work, Games The list of mini folders. Each has a name and an optional path
Folder path empty Leave empty to use %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders\<name>. Any existing folder works, and environment variables are expanded
Position in the taskbar Next to the Start button Can also be after the last taskbar app, or at the far left edge of the taskbar
Mini folder button size 40 Size of the tile, from 28 to 56
Icons per row in the opened folder 4 Width of the panel, from 1 to 10 icons

Renaming a mini folder that uses the default path points it to a new, empty folder. The old folder and its contents stay on disk.

Files and folders the mod creates

  • The folder of a mini folder (by default inside %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders), created when you first use + Add... or Open folder in it.
  • The shortcuts that + Add... puts into that folder.

These are your files. The mod never deletes them, so they stay on disk after the mod is disabled or removed. Delete the TaskbarFolders folder yourself if you no longer need it.

Performance

  • Folder contents and icons are read on a background thread, never on the taskbar thread, so a slow disk or a network folder can't freeze the taskbar.
  • Nothing runs in the background: no timers and no folder watching. The tile preview is refreshed when you open the mini folder or change it from the panel.
  • Opening the same mini folder again reuses the icons that are already loaded.

Limitations

  • Windows 11 with the new taskbar only. It doesn't work with the old taskbar restored by ExplorerPatcher or similar tools.
  • If you change a folder in Explorer, the tile preview updates the next time you open that mini folder.
  • Dragging items onto a mini folder is not supported. Use + Add... or Open folder.
  • The panel does not scroll. A folder with many items gets more icons per row so that the panel fits the screen. Items that still don't fit are not shown.

Tip: unpin the normal taskbar icons and keep everything in mini folders.

entry.title: Yandex Music Transparency 1.1
entry.content:
Yandex Music Transparency

Automatically makes the Yandex Music (Яндекс Музыка.exe) desktop window transparent on startup and continuously prevents the Electron application from resetting its opacity or removing WS_EX_LAYERED.

Unlike one-shot rule-based or hotkey-based opacity mods, this mod injects into the process to actively preserve your chosen transparency level across window state changes and redraws.

Settings

  • Window Opacity (Alpha): Controls the opacity level from 50 (more transparent) to 255 (fully opaque). Default is 220.

Using with other applications

Although tailored for Yandex Music by default, you can apply the same persistent transparency to other Chromium/Electron applications by adding their executable names in the mod's Advanced tab under Custom process inclusion list.

Limitations

  • Only affects top-level windows with the Chrome_WidgetWin_1 window class.
  • Windows that already use color-key transparency (LWA_COLORKEY) are skipped to avoid visual artifacts.
  • Disabling or unloading the mod restores the window's original opacity and layered style.

Credits

Created with assistance from ChatGPT.

entry.title: WindowPilot 1.2.0
entry.content:
WindowPilot

English

Control the foreground window with configurable shortcuts:

Default shortcut Action
Win + Q Close normally, preserving the application's save prompts
Win + Z Minimize
Win + N Maximize; optionally restore when already maximized
Win + Shift + N Open the native Windows Notification Center
Win + S Original Windows Search, unchanged

Each window action has independent enable, shortcut, game protection and double-press confirmation settings. Game protection is enabled by default; double-press confirmation is disabled by default. Shortcuts support Win, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24 and common named keys. Examples: Win+Q, Ctrl+Alt+F10, Win+Shift+N. Only the exact configured combination is consumed. Changing or disabling a shortcut immediately releases its old combination. Win+S and Win+L are reserved; duplicate or invalid bindings show a warning.

With confirmation enabled, press and release the shortcut twice in less than 3 seconds. The hint disappears after 1.5 seconds by default; its disappearance does not shorten the confirmation deadline. Holding a key never confirms. Switching windows, choosing another action, pressing Esc or saving settings cancels a pending confirmation. Timings are configurable for each action.

Hint appearance: automatically follows the Windows display language in English, Portuguese or Spanish, with English fallback for other languages. You can also select a language manually. Dark and light themes can follow Windows or be selected explicitly. Always on top is configurable and enabled by default. The hint never steals keyboard focus or intercepts clicks. Settings labels follow the language selected in the Windhawk interface.

Compatibility: Windows 11 x64 and Windhawk 1.7.3 or later. WindowPilot runs in a dedicated Windhawk tool process for standard desktop windows. Elevated apps and secure-desktop prompts are outside the supported scope.

Games: detection uses editable executable/path patterns, Unity/Unreal window classes and optional fullscreen geometry. It is conservative: browser F11 fullscreen can be protected too; ordinary maximized windows are excluded from the fullscreen heuristic. Add unrecognized windowed games to the list. When game protection applies, the original Windows shortcut receives the key. The same applies on the desktop, taskbar, menus and windows that cannot perform the requested action. On eligible windows, the defaults take over Windows Search (Win+Q), Snap layouts (Win+Z) and Notification Center (Win+N). Use Win+S for Search, Win+Shift+N for notifications, or change the assignments to use the original combinations.

Notifications use the original Win+N after the alternate shortcut's modifiers are released. Tagged synthetic input prevents recursive maximization. If an existing Windows policy disables Notification Center, the hint explains the restriction. Closing a window sends a normal close request to the application.

Português

Atalhos padrão: Win+Q fecha, Win+Z minimiza, Win+N maximiza/restaura, Win+Shift+N abre notificações e Win+S continua sendo a pesquisa nativa. Cada ação tem opções independentes de ativação, atalho, proteção para jogos e duas pressões. A proteção para jogos vem ativada e a confirmação desativada.

Com a confirmação ligada, solte a tecla e pressione novamente em menos de 3 segundos. O aviso some após 1,5 segundo, mas o prazo continua válido. Trocar de janela, usar outra ação, pressionar Esc ou salvar configurações cancela.

Em Aparência do aviso, escolha idioma automático/inglês/português/espanhol, tema automático/escuro/claro e Sempre no topo. O modo automático acompanha o idioma de exibição e o tema do Windows; o aviso não captura foco nem cliques. Os rótulos das configurações seguem o idioma da interface do Windhawk.

Compatível com Windows 11 x64 e Windhawk 1.7.3 ou posterior. O mod roda em um processo dedicado do Windhawk para janelas comuns. Aplicativos elevados e a área de trabalho segura ficam fora da cobertura. Use o botão do Windhawk para desativar o mod inteiro.

Para jogos protegidos, área de trabalho, barra de tarefas, menus ou janelas que não aceitam a ação, vale o atalho original do Windows. Em janelas compatíveis, os padrões substituem Pesquisa (Win+Q), layouts de encaixe (Win+Z) e Central de Notificações (Win+N). Use Win+S para pesquisar, Win+Shift+N para notificações ou mude as combinações para recuperar os atalhos originais. Se uma política do Windows bloquear a Central de Notificações, o aviso indica a restrição.

Español

Atajos predeterminados: Win+Q cierra, Win+Z minimiza, Win+N maximiza/restaura, Win+Shift+N abre notificaciones y Win+S conserva la búsqueda de Windows. Cada acción tiene controles independientes para activar, cambiar el atajo, ignorar juegos y exigir dos pulsaciones. La protección para juegos está activada; la confirmación está desactivada de forma predeterminada.

Con la confirmación activada, suelta la tecla y pulsa de nuevo en menos de 3 segundos. El aviso desaparece después de 1,5 segundos, pero el plazo sigue vigente. Cambiar de ventana, usar otra acción, pulsar Esc o guardar ajustes cancela.

En Apariencia del aviso, elige idioma automático/inglés/portugués/español, tema automático/oscuro/claro y Siempre visible. El modo automático sigue el idioma de visualización y el tema de Windows. El aviso no roba foco ni clics. Los ajustes siguen el idioma elegido en la interfaz de Windhawk.

Compatible con Windows 11 x64 y Windhawk 1.7.3 o posterior. El mod se ejecuta en un proceso dedicado de Windhawk para ventanas normales. Las aplicaciones elevadas y el escritorio seguro quedan fuera del alcance. Usa el interruptor de Windhawk para desactivar todo el mod.

En juegos protegidos, el escritorio, la barra de tareas, los menús o ventanas que no admiten la acción, se conserva el atajo original de Windows. En ventanas compatibles, los valores predeterminados sustituyen Búsqueda (Win+Q), diseños de acoplamiento (Win+Z) y Centro de notificaciones (Win+N). Usa Win+S para buscar, Win+Shift+N para las notificaciones o cambia las combinaciones para recuperar los atajos originales. Un aviso indica si una directiva de Windows bloquea el Centro de notificaciones.

entry.title: Tray Ghost Icon Cleaner 1.0
entry.content:
Tray Ghost Icon Cleaner

For Windows 10 and older Windows 11 versions. Newer Windows 11 versions with the new (XAML) notification area already track the owner processes and remove these icons themselves, so the mod isn't needed there. See Compatibility.

When a program crashes or is terminated, it never removes its notification area (tray) icon. Explorer only notices that the owner is gone when the mouse passes over the icon, so "ghost" icons and duplicates pile up until you hover over the tray.

How it works

Programs add and remove tray icons with Shell_NotifyIcon, which delivers each request to the taskbar window as a WM_COPYDATA message. The mod watches those messages inside Explorer, together with Explorer's answer to each of them, so it knows exactly which icon belongs to which process — including icons identified by GUID — without reading any internal Explorer data.

  • For every process that owns an icon, the mod registers a wait on the process handle (no polling).
  • When the process exits, the mod waits 1.5 s and then removes the icons that are still there with a regular Shell_NotifyIcon(NIM_DELETE), using the same identity (window + ID, or GUID) the program registered them with. An icon is only removed when the window it belongs to is gone as well.
  • A light 30 s check catches owners the mod couldn't open or wait on: it only looks at its own list, not at the tray.
  • When the mod is loaded together with Explorer (the usual case), it sees every icon from the start. When it is enabled while Explorer is already running, it learns the existing icons the next time their program updates them (tooltip, image or state). Optionally, it can send the documented TaskbarCreated notification once so that running programs re-register their icons right away. Every program receives it as if Explorer had restarted, so it's off by default.
  • Every removed ghost is logged — program path, PID and tooltip — to the Windhawk log and, optionally, to ghosts.log in the mod's storage folder (its full path is written to the Windhawk log), so you can find out which program keeps leaving them.

Compared to other approaches

This mod Tray refresh utilities Tray reset tools Restarting Explorer
Runs as part of Explorer, no extra process separate background program one-off program manual
Trigger the owner process exiting timer or on demand when you run it when you do it
Method NIM_DELETE with the icon's own identity simulated mouse moves over the tray, or reading Explorer's toolbar memory from another process resets the tray settings in the registry full restart
Icons registered by GUID removed (if the mod was enabled while Explorer was running: once their program has updated them) depends on the tool — removed
Tells you who left the icon yes, program and PID no no no
Side effects none by default; the optional TaskbarCreated on load reaches every program, as if Explorer had restarted depends on the tool; may lag behind clears your icon visibility settings taskbar flickers, open Explorer windows close

Compatibility

  • Windows 10 — tested on 22H2.
  • Older Windows 11 versions whose notification area still behaves like Windows 10's, and Windows 11 with the Windows 10 taskbar restored.
  • Not needed on newer Windows 11 versions with the XAML notification area: Explorer there tracks the processes that own tray icons and removes the icons itself.

entry.title: Change More Fonts 1.0.0
entry.content:
Change More Fonts

Pick an installed font under Settings > Font > Font family. The default is Tahoma. The mod keeps the size requested by Windows. You can keep the requested weight or set your own. Some fonts take up more room, so labels may wrap or cut off sooner.

Where it applies

Area Text the mod can change
File Explorer File names, details, navigation pane, address bar, and context menus
Desktop Icon labels and menus
Taskbar Labels, tooltips, and menus
Start and Search Menu text, app labels, and the search box
Quick Settings and notification center Labels and buttons
Windows Settings Page headings, row labels, and descriptions
Touch keyboard and input UI Labels drawn by the Windows input host
Classic controls in these processes Menus, tooltips, status bars, and dialogs

Coverage depends on how each control draws text. DWM title bars, web content, and text rendered as images are outside the supported paths. The mod skips icon fonts, emoji, and some fonts used for specific scripts. With classic controls, pick a font that has the characters you need, since GDI fallback is limited.

Screenshots

Windows Settings

Mod off Zen Maru Gothic

Explorer details view

Mod off Tahoma

Changing more fonts

The default list covers the usual Windows UI families. Add specific families under Also replace these fonts or turn on Replace all eligible fonts to include document fonts such as Arial and Calibri. Turn on Include monospace fonts if you want the same rules to apply to fonts such as Consolas. The Keep these fonts list takes priority.

To try a different app, add its executable under this mod's Advanced > Process inclusion list. The app needs to use GDI or system DirectWrite for its text. Use the per-mod exclusion list to skip apps.

Compatibility

Run one font replacement mod at a time. If you use Explorer Font Changer, disable it before enabling Change More Fonts.

Taskbar, Start menu, and notification center stylers can assign fonts to individual controls. If a theme's font should stay, add its family to Keep these fonts. To use your chosen family on that control, update the theme's font rule or add its family to Also replace these fonts.

Explorer Translucent Menus and Translucent Windows also hook classic text drawing. If menu text looks wrong with either mod enabled, try Rendering > Keep cached GDI fonts. Font creation and DirectWrite changes still work with that option on.

Windows font substitutions you set separately can still affect GDI text with Change More Fonts paused.

Refresh the text

Restart the affected app if it still shows the old font. Signing out and back in refreshes Start and other shell processes. Restarting also helps if text is clipped because the app measured it with a cached font. Turning the mod off and restarting the affected app restores its usual font.

The mod runs in 64-bit processes on Windows 11 and changes fonts in memory. Optional apps added through the inclusion list also need to be 64-bit.

entry.title: Fluent Radial Menu 0.9.0
entry.content:
Fluent Radial Menu

Fluent Radial Menu adds a circular launcher to Windows 11. It comes with three pages of apps, folders, Windows shortcuts, and screen capture tools.

Getting started

  1. Enable the mod in Windhawk and press Ctrl+Alt+Space to open the wheel at the pointer. To change the shortcut, set Activation shortcut in the mod's Windhawk settings and click Save settings.
  2. Click a wedge to run its action. Scroll to switch pages or press Esc to dismiss the wheel. You can also use the arrow keys, Enter, and Page Up or Page Down.
  3. Press F2 while the wheel is open, or right-click it and choose Edit radial menu, to open the built-in editor.

The wheel stays closed while the foreground app is fullscreen.

Screen capture tools

Choose Color picker on the first page to open the capture toolbar at the top center of the display under the pointer. Use the toolbar to switch to Copy text from screen. In the color picker, the magnifier shows the exact pixel under the pointer, its #RRGGBB value, and its screen coordinates. Click to copy that color, or drag around text in the text tool. A confirmation appears after copying. Press Esc to cancel. Text recognition runs locally using Windows OCR and the recognition languages installed for your account.

To add either tool to an existing layout, select a wedge in Actions and choose it from Action type.

Make it yours

  • Actions lets you choose an installed app, folder, file, website, Windows settings page, keyboard shortcut, command, or capture tool. Select Custom… to browse for a local target. Choose the original app icon, a built-in symbol, or an icon file. Drag a wedge in the preview to move or swap it.
  • Pages lets you add, rename, reorder, or duplicate up to eight pages with eight slots each.
  • Appearance controls the theme, accent, size, transparency, blur, and labels. Motion & activation controls the profile shortcut, positioning, and animation. It can follow Windows' reduced motion setting.
  • Apply saves your changes. Test on desktop opens the applied wheel with actions disabled.

Share or back up a layout

Export profile saves the current editor layout and settings as JSON. Import profile opens a profile in the editor. Review its actions and select Apply when you are ready to use it. Shared profiles reference apps, folders, and custom icon files by path, so those may need to be updated on another PC. The built-in icons travel with the profile.

A shortcut set in Windhawk takes priority over the profile shortcut. Clear the Windhawk field to use the profile shortcut again. In Motion & activation, focus Profile shortcut and press the middle button or either side button to record it. Hold any modifiers you want to include, then click Apply. A mouse shortcut toggles the wheel. Hold keyboard shortcut to select applies to keyboard activation. Check the Windhawk mod log if Windows cannot register a new shortcut.

On 64-bit Windows, the menu opens native system apps from either Windhawk host. In the 32-bit file picker, enter %WINDIR%\Sysnative in the address bar to browse the native System32 folder. The editor saves those selections as System32 paths so the same profile works in the 64-bit host.

entry.title: Taskbar Position Shortcut 0.1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Position Shortcut

Adds a Taskbar position submenu when you right-click the Windows 11 taskbar. Choose a global position for this Explorer session, or set a position for a specific app.

Finally, Windows brought back a feature they thought was not being used. I prefer my taskbar on the left when working in Photoshop, and on top when scrolling through layers in After Effects.

Features

  • Global position: Choose Follow Windows setting, Top, Left, Right, or Bottom. This lasts for the current Explorer session and does not save an app rule.
  • Per-app positions: Open the app's submenu to save a position that overrides the global choice. Choose Default to use the global position.
  • Maximized-only mode: Only apply app rules when a maximized window is found.
  • Switch delay: Adjust how long the mod waits before moving the taskbar.
  • Blacklist: Ignore apps you don't want triggering position changes.

App rules are saved locally in Windhawk and won't appear in its Settings tab.

Compatibility

Requires Windows 11 with native taskbar positioning. I've tried it on builds 26220.9836 and 26300.9818. Older builds haven't been tested. I've only tested it with one monitor.

The mod doesn't change the saved Windows taskbar position. It may conflict with other mods that move the taskbar.

Credits: Taskbar menu injection based on taskbar-restart-explorer; runtime position hooking based on taskbar-on-top.

entry.title: File Explorer List view indent fix and files area spacing 1.0
entry.content:
File Explorer List view indent fix and files area spacing

Starting with Windows 11 version 22H2, File Explorer reserves a 28 pixels wide area to the left of every item in the List, Small icons and Content views. The area is meant for sync status icons of cloud folders (OneDrive and other sync providers), but it's reserved in every folder, including the folders which have nothing to do with the cloud. The result is an odd indent between the edge of an item and its icon.

The mod removes that area where there's nothing to show. It also fixes a number of smaller spacing inconsistencies in the files area. Every adjustment has a setting, and can be changed or turned off.

The mod only deals with the files area: the part of a folder window which shows the files and the folders. It doesn't touch the navigation pane, the command bar or the address bar.

Before and after

All the files are selected in the screenshots, to show the gaps around the items. The top half of each image is without the mod, the bottom half is with the mod and its default settings.

List

Small icons

Content

Details

Tiles

What it does

  • No empty status area. The reserved area is removed where there's nothing to show. Items which have a status icon, and all the items inside of a cloud folder, still have it, so the status icons keep working and stay aligned. Optionally, the status icons can be hidden in the List and Small icons views altogether.
  • Even gaps around an item. The gap between the border of an item and its content is the same on the left and on the right, in the List, Small icons, Tiles, Content and Details views. The size of the gap is configurable. The right gap of the List view has a correction of its own.
  • Narrower status icon area. The same gap is used on both sides of a status icon, also in the Tiles and Content views.
  • Icon and name. A configurable gap is added between the item icon and the name, the same in the List, Small icons and Details views. The names and the status icons can be moved vertically. The Small icons view has a separate offset for the names.
  • Rows of the Details view. The gap between the icon and the name is made the same as in the List view. A negative offset of the names is taken from the height of the rows, so that the names stay centered in the rows.
  • Rows of the Content view. The padding below the text of a row is configurable.
  • Even margins around the files area. The files area gets margins on all four sides, in all views. The horizontal and the vertical margins are configurable separately.

Defaults

Only the removal of the empty status area is a fix in the strict sense. The other adjustments are a matter of taste, and they're turned on by default too. To get the stock look of a part back, use these values:

  • Even item spacing: off. That also turns off the gaps and the offsets of the icons and the names, and the adjustments of the Details and Content rows.
  • Horizontal and vertical margins of the files area: 0.

Scaling

The gaps, the paddings and the margins follow the display scaling. The vertical offsets and the correction of the right gap are small corrections of a pixel or two, and are applied in physical pixels regardless of the scaling.

Items which are already displayed when the display scaling changes keep the old spacing until the folder is reopened or refreshed. With fractional scaling such as 125%, the gaps can differ by a pixel because of rounding.

The mod works with the compact view of File Explorer turned on or off, and with the item check boxes.

Other programs

By default, the mod only applies to File Explorer (explorer.exe). That's the recommended setup, and nothing has to be configured for it.

The same items view is used by the Open/Save dialogs of other programs. To fix it there too, add the programs to the custom process inclusion list in the Advanced tab of the mod, by the name of the executable file, for example notepad.exe. explorer.exe doesn't have to be added, it's always included.

It's also possible to add *, which means all programs. The mod is then loaded into every process, including the ones which never show a file dialog, so adding only the programs you need is the lighter option.

Only 64-bit programs are supported. In a program other than File Explorer, the mod does nothing until the program loads the items view (explorerframe.dll), which usually happens when a file dialog is opened for the first time.

How it works

The indent comes from UIProperty::HasVisibleContent in explorerframe.dll, which reports the status icons area as having content in the List, Small icons and Content views regardless of the actual content. The mod makes it report the actual state.

Everything else is done by changing properties of DirectUI elements: of the items and of the items area. The elements are adjusted when they're created, and the windows which are already open are adjusted when the mod is loaded. The functions which are exported by dui70.dll are used for that.

No files are modified. The adjustments are only made to elements which have the expected stock values, so that the mod stays out of the way of other customizations. When the mod is turned off, the stock values are restored.

The code of the status area fix was verified to have the expected shape in Windows 11 builds 22621.317 - 22621.6274 (22H2, 23H2), 26100.1 - 26100.9974 (24H2, 25H2), 28000.1761 - 28000.3086 (26H1) and 26300 (26H2 preview). The adjustments of the Details view rows were tested on build 26300 at 125% scaling.

entry.title: Explorer: No Help 1.0
entry.content:
Explorer: No Help

For Windows 10 File Explorer (the ribbon one).

Before:

After:

  • Hide Help button: Explorer's ribbon ships pre-compiled inside SystemResources\ExplorerFrame.dll.mun (resource UIFILE/EXPLORER_RIBBON). When the ribbon framework loads it, this mod hands back a patched copy with the tabs_help block (the ? button) removed, the same result as if Microsoft had compiled the ribbon without a help button. Nothing on disk is touched.
  • Block F1: swallows bare F1 inside explorer.exe (folder windows, desktop, taskbar). Ctrl/Shift/Alt+F1 still go through, so Ctrl+F1 still collapses the ribbon. F1 in every other app is left alone.

Restart Explorer after enabling the mod or toggling the Help button setting. The F1 setting takes effect immediately.

If anything about the ribbon binary doesn't look exactly as expected, the patch bails out and logs why, and Explorer gets the original ribbon.

Special thanks to d0gkiller87, whose F1 Blocker the F1 part copies, and to DarkShadow44’s reverse-engineering notes on UIRibbon.

entry.title: AI Text Assistant (?fix, ?formal, ?emojify, ?undo) 2.4.0
entry.content:
AI Text Assistant (?fix, ?formal, ?emojify, ?undo, ...)

Transform, polish, or rewrite your text anywhere in Windows simply by typing a quick command at the end of any text box.

Works across chat apps, emails, web browsers, documents, social media, and forms.

Instant Commands (Type at the end of your text)

Command What it does Example input
?fix Fixes spelling, grammar, punctuation, and clarity She dont has no time for that ?fix
?formal Rewrites in a professional, polite business tone cant make it to the meeting today ?formal
?casual Rewrites in a friendly, conversational tone I am writing to inquire regarding your plans ?casual
?short Makes your message concise, crisp, and to the point Due to the fact that it is raining heavily outside right now ?short
?emojify Enriches your text with expressive, fitting emojis Super excited for the weekend party ?emojify
?undo Instantly reverts back to your original text ?undo

(You can type commands with or without a space, e.g., ?fix or ? fix).

Instant Undo & Cancellation

  • During AI generation: Press Esc at any time to immediately cancel and keep your original text untouched.
  • After AI generation: If you don't like the AI's result, simply type ?undo (or ? undo) in the text field to immediately revert back to your original text.

Free API Key Setup (No credit card required)

Get a free key from either provider below and paste it into the mod settings:

  • Google Gemini (Recommended): Get free Gemini API Key
  • Groq: Get free Groq API Key

Auto-Verification: As soon as you paste your key and save settings, the mod automatically tests the connection in the background and confirms it is working.

Safety & Privacy

  • What Data is Sent: When you type an active trigger (e.g. ?fix, ?formal), the text content of the active field (whatever Select All selects, up to the configured max_chars limit, 4,000 characters by default) is sent over an encrypted HTTPS connection directly to your chosen AI provider (generativelanguage.googleapis.com for Google Gemini, or api.groq.com for Groq). When you add or change an API key in settings, a brief connection test request sending the word "Hi" is performed to verify your key.
  • Provider Terms & Data Handling: Because this mod uses your own direct API key with the provider, each provider's respective privacy policy and terms of service apply. For example, on Google Gemini's free tier, Google's terms state that submitted content may be used to improve products and may be reviewed by human reviewers. Groq's data retention and privacy policies apply when using Groq.
  • Clipboard History & Cloud Sync: Reading the field uses Ctrl+C, so each time you use a command, the field's full text is added to your clipboard history (Win+V) and, if clipboard sync is set to automatic, synced to your other devices. However, during the replacement paste and when restoring your previous clipboard content, the mod applies Windows exclusion formats (ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing, CanIncludeInClipboardHistory, and CanUploadToCloudClipboard) so that intermediate changes and restored clipboard data are not duplicated into clipboard history or synced across devices.
  • Accidental Typing Protection: While the AI processes your request, keyboard input in the target window is safely paused so typed keystrokes do not interfere with processing. You can cancel any in-flight request at any time by pressing Esc. If you switch to another window or app while the AI is thinking, input in your other window is never blocked.
  • Terminal Protection: Command prompts and terminal windows (PowerShell, Command Prompt, Windows Terminal, ConHost, MinTTY, PuTTY, ConEmu) are excluded by class and process so shortcuts and triggers never interfere with console sessions.
  • Document Protection: Fields longer than the configured maximum character limit (max_chars) are left untouched to protect large open files and documents.
  • Dedicated Background Process: This mod runs safely as a dedicated Windhawk tool mod, isolating network and keyboard handling from explorer.exe to protect your taskbar and desktop stability.

entry.title: File Type Properties Customization 1.0.0
entry.content:
File Type Properties Customization

Customize file icons and type descriptions by extension. Icons and descriptions can be enabled independently. File associations, default applications, and system thumbnail providers are preserved.

Before:

After:

Windhawk settings

Fill in the first File type properties entry, then save settings. For example:

  • Extensions: .txt,.log
  • Icon: %SystemRoot%\System32\shell32.dll,70
  • Description: Text document

Either property may be left empty to keep the preset or system value. A completely empty entry ends the list; entries below it are ignored. Windhawk's Textual mode can edit the same settings as YAML.

Optional INI preset

Enable Load INI preset and select an absolute INI path. The preset is read first; nonempty valid Windhawk settings override individual properties afterward.

[.txt,.log]
Icon=icons\text.ico
Description=Text document

[.log]
Description=Log file

Sections and keys are case-insensitive. Repeated sections merge per property in file order. Empty or invalid values do not erase earlier usable values. Relative resource paths use the INI directory; paths in settings must be absolute. Paths support environment variables. Quote icon paths containing commas. Icon indexes start at 0; negative indexes select resource IDs. Descriptions also accept @module,-resourceID, or @@ to start literal text with @.

Save INI files as UTF-8, or UTF-16 LE with BOM. Full-line comments start with ; or #. After editing the INI, re-enable the mod or save a changed mod setting. The file is not watched automatically.

Refresh and limitations

  • Refresh Explorer when mappings change is off by default. Enabling it may redraw windows and reload thumbnails after changed mappings are saved, including the first or last rule. An empty configuration stays loaded without hooks while this option is on. Startup and shutdown do not request a refresh.
  • Reopen affected windows or menus if they still show cached values.
  • Prefer local icon files. First use of a slow or disconnected network resource can block the requesting window until Windows finishes trying to load it.
  • By default, only explorer.exe is targeted. For an application's standard Open/Save dialogs, add its executable to Custom process inclusion list and restart it. Applications with their own rendering or caches may be unaffected.
  • Description overrides cover supported Type columns, file properties, details, and native Shell New menus. If optional Shell symbols are unavailable, some views keep system descriptions; details are logged.
  • x86, x64, and ARM64 are targeted. ARM64 has not been tested on a physical device.

entry.title: Windows 10 IME Tray Icon Fix 1.1
entry.content:
Windows 10 IME Tray Icon Fix

Default Stock Layout And The Bug

  Screen Left  <-----------------------------------------------------  Screen Right Edge
  [Chevron ^]  |  [SysPager (Tray Icons)]  |  [IME Indicator]  |  [Clock]  |  [Show Desktop]

The notification area (TrayNotifyWnd) is anchored to the right edge of the screen, while child windows are laid out left-to-right. Notice that the IME Indicator sits right in the middle, between the third-party tray icons (SysPager) and the clock.

When "Let me set a different input method for each app window" is enabled in a multilingual setup (e.g., English, Chinese, Japanese):

  1. While typing in an app, the indicator often displays 2 glyphs (e.g., CH + 中 or JP + あ), occupying a wider slot.
  2. When you click a tray icon (such as Steam or WiFi), WM_LBUTTONDOWN immediately shifts focus to explorer.exe.
  3. The shell defaults to English, shrinking the indicator down to 1 glyph (ENG).
  4. Because the clock on the right is pinned to the right edge, the shrunk width forces everything to the left of the indicator (SysPager and Chevron ^) to slide rightward.
  5. When WM_LBUTTONUP fires, the icon you aimed at has moved, and your click lands on whichever neighboring icon slid under your cursor.

The Fix

Each can solve the bug alone, but you can customize the taskbar by enabling multiple modes!

Mode 1: Move the input indicator to the leftmost (recommended)

[IME Indicator]  |  [Chevron ^]  |  [SysPager (Tray Icons)]  |  [Clock]  |  [Show Desktop]

The indicator takes the first slot and everything that used to sit left of it moves right by the indicator's width. Thus, every band is now to the right of the indicator, sits at a fixed distance from the right edge and never moves.

Mimicking Docked Language Bar?

Yes. But the docked language bar is broken in win10 (unstable, and won't work in remote desktop - even if you enable this option in both sides, and the latest MSPY doesn't support it unless you turn on "Use the old version of MSPY") and is completely removed in win11.

Mode 2: Fixed width

Forces the indicator to always occupy a fixed width. The value is in pixels at 100% display scaling and is scaled by the monitor DPI. 36 = one glyph, 58 = glyph + secondary. Other values accepted too.

Mode 3: Hide secondary IME mode glyph (single-glyph mode)

Hides the 中/英 or あ/Ａ button inside the indicator.

Notes and known limitations

  • Source code and reverse engineering credit goes to AI bot (deepseek v4.1 flash).
  • Heavily guided and reviewed by human (the author) to ensure the minimal path and minimal overhead. (The bots used extra threads, timers...)
  • Tested on Windows 10 21H2. Windows 10 20H2 and above (including LTSC 2021, Builds 19042–19045) share the exact same binary codebase, so it should work flawlessly. Earlier builds (1903/1909 and prior) should theoretically work as well, but remain untested.

entry.title: No-Click Touchpad: Tap & Hold 1.0
entry.content:
No-Click Touchpad: Tap & Hold

Right-click and drag with taps and holds, for touchpads whose click no longer works. It's also handy if you'd rather tap than press.

Right-click

Tap the bottom right corner of the touchpad with one finger to right-click. You can switch to the bottom left corner in the mod's settings. Without the mod, a tap in that corner is a normal left click.

Drag

Rest two fingers on the touchpad and keep them still for a moment. A ring appears around the pointer to show that a drag has started. Move your fingers to select text or move a window, and lift them to let go.

To scroll, move two fingers straight away instead of holding them still first. Pinching or rotating two fingers won't start a drag.

On a small touchpad, a long drag can run out of room. Set "Time to reposition fingers" in the mod's settings to keep the drag going for a moment after you lift your fingers, so you can put them back down and carry on. During that moment, a one-finger tap ends the drag right away.

Requirements

The touchpad has to be a Precision Touchpad, which most laptops from the last several years have. Some older touchpads aren't supported.

In Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad, keep "Tap with a single finger to single-click" on, since the corner right-click needs it. Turning off "Tap twice and drag" there is recommended, because with it on Windows waits a moment after every tap to see whether a drag follows. If letting go of a two-finger hold too early opens a menu, turn off "Tap with two fingers to right-click" as well.

If you also use the Touchpad Relaxed Hand Tracking mod, turn off its two-finger option so the two mods don't both react to the same gesture.

Limitations

While you drag, some apps may still scroll a little, and a mouse wheel doesn't scroll.

On Windhawk 1.x, neither the right-click nor the drag works in apps running as administrator. On a regular (not portable) install of Windhawk 2.0, both work there too.

Issues

Bugs and feature requests go on the issues page.

entry.title: !Net — Per-App Kill Switch 1.2026.1510
entry.content:
Screenshots

Two Modes

  • Session-Only (Floating Pill / Panel, default): Uses Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) dynamic sessions (FWPM_SESSION_DYNAMIC). Blocks vanish automatically on Windows restart, shutdown, or when !Net exits or crashes.
  • Auto-Blocked Rules: Saved in Mod Settings (autoBlockedApps) and applied automatically via WFP dynamic sessions (FWPM_SESSION_DYNAMIC) whenever !Net starts, vanishing cleanly on exit.

Direction Modes

  • Offline (Fully offline): Blocks incoming + outgoing traffic (default).
  • Outbound (Can't reach internet): Blocks outgoing connections only.
  • Inbound (Can't be reached): Blocks incoming connections only.

Shortcuts

Icon Shortcut / Trigger Action
⚡ Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1 Toggle block/allow for foreground app (! key)
◧ Ctrl+Alt+Shift+M Expand / collapse floating pill
↺ Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R Restore all (clear session blocks)

Cycle Mode

  • Trigger: Double-click an app row (or right-click → Cycle...) — enabled by default in Settings.
  • Schedule: Alternates Blocked → Allowed (min | sec, optional ms in Settings) using the row's direction. Run Until stopped, For N cycles, or For a set time (supports Sync with Windows clock in 12h/24h).
  • Focus & Session: Only while app is focused freezes the timer on focus loss; Allow internet when out of focus keeps the app online in the background while paused. Per-app Cycle templates are remembered inside Windhawk storage (without auto-starting); active cycles remain session-only and wipe on app exit/crash, !Net exit, or Windows restart.

Filter Chips

  • Allowed / Blocked: Click Blocked again to switch between !Net blocks and Blocked · FW (external Windows Defender Firewall rules).
  • Running / User: Click Running again to toggle active-window/network apps vs. all running user apps. Locked system apps and Blocked · FW apps are hidden from Running by default (toggle Show non-manageable apps in Running in Settings).
  • System / Excluded: View Windows system processes or restore excluded apps.

Permissions & Safety

  • Administrator Rights: Modifying WFP session filters requires elevation (via windhawk-mod-elevated.exe on Windhawk 2.0, or on-demand UAC elevation of windhawk.exe -tool-mod on Windhawk 1.7.3).
  • Immutable Security & Core OS Protection: Core Windows processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, services.exe, csrss.exe, winlogon.exe, smss.exe, wininit.exe), Windhawk hosts (windhawk.exe, windhawk-mod.exe, windhawk-mod-elevated.exe), Windows Defender / SmartScreen (MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe, MpCmdRun.exe, MpDefenderCoreService.exe, SecurityHealthService.exe, SmartScreen.exe), and major third-party AV/EDR processes are permanently protected even if Lock system-critical processes is turned off.
  • Session & User Isolation: Session 0 services (SessionId == 0) and processes belonging only to other Windows user accounts are isolated, locked, and hidden from Running / Allowed by default so !Net only manages the active interactive user's session processes.
  • Warns before blocking remote desktop or VPN clients when an active remote session or VPN process is detected.

entry.title: Nimbus Menu 1.0.0
entry.content:
Nimbus Menu

Replaces the Windows taskbar with a light dock, one per monitor, with its own Start menu.

  • Floating dock or full-width bar; 4 looks (Névoa, Cristal, Grafite, Aurora).
  • macOS-like zoom (or Lift / Focus), live window previews (hover a thumbnail to peek), drag icons to reorder, pin and unpin.
  • Its own Start: pinned apps, all apps, app search, files (with Everything or Windows Search) and Windows Settings pages. Compact or wide search.
  • The Windows key opens Nimbus' Start over any window (administrator ones too) and in games. Ctrl+Esc still opens Windows' Start. An optional shortcut (Alt+Space or Ctrl+Space) can open it too.
  • Per-monitor settings: format, auto-hide, what shows, only that monitor's windows.
  • The dock runs in its own Windhawk process and hides when a game or video is in full screen. Explorer only gets one small hook, for the Windows key.
  • The text is in English, or in Portuguese when Windows is in Portuguese.

What it changes in Windows. With "Hide the Windows taskbar" on (the default), the whole Windows taskbar is hidden, so its tray, clock and quick settings are gone too: use another mod or app for those if you need them. To stop the hidden taskbar from reserving screen space, the mod turns on the taskbar's own "Automatically hide the taskbar" option, which Windows saves in your profile. The mod remembers your original choice and puts it back when it's turned off, also after a crash or a shutdown with the mod on. If the Windows taskbar ever stays hidden, turn the mod off or restart Explorer.

Português

Troca a barra de tarefas do Windows por uma dock leve, uma por monitor, com Iniciar próprio.

  • Dock flutuante ou barra fixa; 4 visuais (Névoa, Cristal, Grafite, Aurora).
  • Zoom como no macOS (ou Elevar / Foco), prévia das janelas ao vivo (parar o mouse na miniatura mostra a janela), arrastar ícones pra reorganizar, fixar e desafixar.
  • Iniciar próprio: fixados, todos os apps, busca de apps, arquivos (com o Everything ou a busca do Windows) e telas das Configurações do Windows. Busca compacta ou larga.
  • A tecla Windows abre o Iniciar do Nimbus em qualquer janela (até de administrador) e em jogos. Ctrl+Esc continua abrindo o Iniciar do Windows. Um atalho opcional (Alt+Espaço ou Ctrl+Espaço) também pode abrir.
  • Ajustes por monitor: formato, esconder sozinha, o que aparece, só as janelas daquele monitor.
  • A dock roda num processo próprio do Windhawk e some quando um jogo ou vídeo está em tela cheia. No Explorador entra só um gancho pequeno, o da tecla Windows.
  • Os textos ficam em inglês, ou em português quando o Windows está em português.

O que muda no Windows. Com "Esconder a barra do Windows" ligado (o padrão), a barra do Windows some inteira, então a bandeja, o relógio e as configurações rápidas somem junto: use outro mod ou app pra isso se precisar. Pra barra escondida não reservar espaço na tela, o mod liga a opção "Ocultar automaticamente a barra de tarefas" do próprio Windows, que fica salva no seu perfil. O mod guarda a sua escolha original e devolve quando é desligado, até depois de um travamento ou de desligar o PC com o mod ligado. Se a barra do Windows ficar escondida, desligue o mod ou reinicie o Explorador.

entry.title: Phone panel for NectarLink 1.0.0
entry.content:
Phone panel for NectarLink

Unofficial. This mod is not made by, affiliated with or endorsed by the NectarLink project. It works with NectarLink, the free, open-source app that links an Android phone with a Windows PC.

It puts your phone in the Start menu's phone panel (the one Phone Link uses):

  • your phone's name, connection and battery
  • quick actions: Find phone, Clipboard, Take photo, Scan doc, Play on phone, Send files
  • Recent: the last items from NectarLink's Timeline (click to open)
  • Clipboard: the last clipboard items (click to copy again)
  • Open NectarLink and NectarLink settings

Requirements

  • Windows 11 (x64) and the NectarLink app for Windows, paired with your phone.
  • In NectarLink, turn on Settings → Local automation API. Without it, Find phone / Clipboard / Take photo / Send files and the footer buttons still work; status, Recent, Clipboard, Scan doc and Play on phone need it.
  • Keep Show mobile device in Start turned on in Windows Settings → Personalization → Start.

How it works

The panel shows NectarLink instead of Phone Link. By default it only does so while NectarLink is installed and has a paired phone; otherwise Phone Link's panel is left alone (the "Replace Phone Link's panel" setting can force it). The phone button next to the search box shows and hides it.

Privacy and safety

  • The mod only talks to NectarLink on this PC (127.0.0.1), using the token NectarLink writes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nectarlink\api-token.json. Nothing is sent anywhere else.
  • Clicking a Recent file opens it only if it's a common photo, video, audio or document type. Anything else (programs, scripts, shortcuts...) is shown in File Explorer instead of being opened. Links open only if they're http(s).
  • Turning the mod off restores the Start menu and Phone Link's panel.

If the panel doesn't appear

Open Windhawk's log for this mod (Details → Log). If it can't find where to attach, it prints the named elements of the Start menu.

NectarLink is a trademark of its project; the name is used here only to say what this mod works with.

entry.title: Network Menu Speed Test 1.0
entry.content:
Network Menu Speed Test

Windows 11's network menu ("Run internet speed test") opens

https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2324916

in the default browser, which redirects to a Bing search page.

This mod intercepts that URL in the shell processes and replaces it with a native flyout. The window, the gauge, the result cards and the speed measurement all live inside the mod: no external application or protocol handler is involved. The test talks to the public Cloudflare speed test endpoints (speed.cloudflare.com), the same stateless endpoints used by the website.

Screenshots

Light theme Dark theme
Desktop Acrylic Results card

Data usage

The test transfers real data with a per-direction budget of 512 MB. Lines at or below ~340 Mbps complete the full 12 s window per direction without reaching the budget; faster lines end the phase once the budget is spent (minimum 4 s window, and the result divides bytes by the time the transfer was actually moving data). Total usage stays under ~1 GB regardless of line speed, and the results card shows the bytes used ("Data used: 762 MB", also included in the clipboard text).

The Start the test automatically setting defaults to auto: the test starts when the flyout opens, except when Windows reports the connection as metered - then the flyout opens idle and waits for a click on Start.

Coexistence: the mod perform-speedtest-redirect intercepts the same URL launches. If both are enabled, whichever mod hooks the launch first wins - disable the other one to keep this mod's flyout.

The flyout opens above the taskbar, on the monitor under the mouse. It closes when you click outside, but never while a measurement is running.

It is keyboard accessible (Tab / Enter / Esc with a WinUI-style focus ring), exposed to screen readers through MSAA (WM_GETOBJECT), and honours the "Animation effects" system setting: with animations off every transition is instant. The error view shrinks the window to fit its content.

Settings

  • Extra URL patterns: additional substrings separated by |.
  • Fall back to the web page: if the flyout cannot start, run the original URL instead of doing nothing.
  • Also intercept browser process launches: catch the network menu launching the browser directly through CreateProcessW. The launch returns ERROR_CANCELLED because no browser process is created; turning it off makes the menu open the browser normally when the shell skips the shell-execute path.
  • Start the test automatically: auto starts the test when the flyout opens, but waits for a click when Windows reports the connection as metered; always starts unconditionally; never always waits for a click.
  • Language: auto (follows the Windows display language), it or en.

Diagnostics go to the Windhawk mod log: enable logging for this mod from its Details page in Windhawk when you need them.

Note: when the network menu launches the browser directly through CreateProcessW, the flyout is shown but process creation returns ERROR_CANCELLED: the hook never reports success without creating the requested browser process.

entry.title: Bluetooth No Sleep 1.0.0
entry.content:
Bluetooth No Sleep (Bluetooth Audio Keep-Alive)

A lightweight Windows background utility and Windhawk tool mod that prevents Bluetooth audio devices (headphones, wireless earbuds, soundbars, DACs, and speakers) from falling asleep, dropping initial playback, or disconnecting during silence.

Why this mod?

Modern Bluetooth audio peripherals employ aggressive power-saving timers:

  1. Initial Audio Truncation: When no audio plays for a few seconds, the device enters a low-power state and shuts off its internal DAC/amplifier. When audio resumes, waking up takes 1-2 seconds, dropping the beginning of system notifications, speech, or media playback.
  2. Pops and Static Bursts: Rapid DAC wakeups often create audible transients, clicks, or static bursts ("pink noise").
  3. Unsolicited Idle Disconnections: Many wireless devices shut down completely after 5 to 10 minutes of silence, forcing manual power cycling.

How it works

This mod uses Windows Audio Session API (WASAPI) Shared Mode to continuously stream an inaudible digital silence buffer (0x00 PCM or sub-audible dither) to the active audio endpoint:

  • Non-Intrusive Shared Mode: Runs alongside your normal applications without monopolizing or locking audio devices.
  • Event-Driven Endpoint Tracking: Uses IMMNotificationClient to monitor device transitions. When your default audio device switches or a Bluetooth headset reconnects, it rebinds automatically without crashes.
  • Near-Zero CPU Overhead: Uses buffer-synchronized wait events and sleep cycles to keep CPU usage below 0.1%.
  • Optional Inactivity Gate: Can automatically pause the keep-alive stream after prolonged user inactivity to allow intentional battery conservation and permit normal Windows system sleep (powercfg /requests).
  • Dedicated Tool Mod: Runs inside windhawk.exe as a dedicated background tool without injecting into or hooking any system processes.

entry.title: Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer

Windows does not provide any registry entries or built-in options to customize the icons or labels of core File Explorer context menu commands. This mod was created to fill that gap cleanly and safely.

Windows 11 Note: This mod customizes the classic File Explorer context menu (accessible via Show more options or Shift+F10, or when the classic context menu is enabled).

Screenshots:

Disabled (Default) Enabled (Customized)

Highlights:

  • Canonical Verb Matching: Identifies core shell commands via IContextMenu::GetCommandString (GCS_VERBW), working across every Windows display language without touching third-party shell extension items.
  • Zero Layout Distortion: Attaches icons cleanly during IContextMenu::QueryContextMenu so native row height, padding, and bold text remain completely untouched.
  • Clear-to-Reset Behavior: Clearing an icon path removes the icon for Open, Delete, Rename, or Properties, while Run as administrator reverts to the native Windows UAC shield.
  • Custom Icon Support: Easily add your own .ico files or use any built-in Windows icon with dll,index syntax.
  • Per-Monitor DPI & Leak-Free Caching: Caches 32-bpp ARGB bitmaps per monitor DPI in memory with zero GDI handle leaks.

Dynamic %file% Placeholder:

Include %file% (or %name%) in any custom label field to dynamically display the right-clicked file, folder, or shortcut target name. Names longer than 30 characters are automatically shortened to the first 30 characters followed by ...:

  • Rename: '%file%' -> Rename: 'Spotify.exe'
  • Open: %file% -> Open: New folder (2)
  • Delete %file% -> Delete Very_Long_File_Name_Over_Thirt...
  • %file% Properties -> report.pdf Properties

Supported Context Menu Items:

  1. Open (open) - Top bold default action (default icon: imageres.dll,-185)
  2. Run as administrator (runas) - UAC elevation action (keeps native UAC shield and default label unless customized)
  3. Delete (delete) - File and folder deletion action (default icon: Full Recycle Bin imageres.dll,-54)
  4. Rename (rename) - Inline rename action (default icon: Clipboard shell32.dll,-16763, default label: Rename: '%file%')
  5. Properties (properties) - Bottom item details action (default icon: imageres.dll,-114)

entry.title: Flip3DComp 2.0
entry.content:
Flip3DComp

Original version by: ALTaleX531

A DirectComposition reimplementation of the Flip3D Window switcher introduced on Windows Vista, for newer versions of Windows. Ported from my repository Flip3DComp

Demo

Live window previews follow the original Flip3D carousel layout and timing.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 versions 1703 and higher
  • Windhawk 1.7.3 or higher

⚠️ Notes

  • The optional Task View override currently uses the Windows 11 Task View activation path on AMD64. It is unavailable on x86, ARM64 & Windows 10.
  • Do not enable more than one Win+Tab replacement. Disable Any mods that override Win+Tab, or leave Win+Tab disabled in Alt+Tab Flip 3D, while using Flip3DComp.

Controls

Mod disclosure
